research.topic: Tea consumption per person: Turkey leads the world at roughly 3.2 kg per person per year (Euromonitor data via Statista; FAO consumption tables), ahead of Ireland (about 2.2 kg) and the United Kingdom (about 1.9 kg); China, the largest producer and total consumer, drinks well under 1 kg per head. Turkey grows nearly all its own tea in Rize and neighbouring provinces on the wet eastern Black Sea coast, through the state company ÇAYKUR and private firms, and is among the world's top five producers. Black tea (çay) is brewed in a stacked double kettle (çaydanlık) and served in small tulip-shaped glasses many times a day.

myths.myth: The British drink more tea than anyone.
myths.reality: Per person, Turkey drinks roughly half as much again as Britain; Ireland also out-drinks the UK. Britain's reputation comes from history, not today's per-head numbers.

landscape.our_gap: Tea-consumption clips are top-10 lists; nobody beats the British guess with to-scale bars, pins the hills where the winner grows its own leaf, and rides the tea across the country to the glass as a quiz.
